messages:
maya: Heads up — GitOps canary failed for a gpupool module bump (provider v3 -> v4). Canary env in us-west-2 couldn't provision new nodes due to a mix of KMS access denied + quota errors. We rolled the canary back and paused merges.

sasha: Which change in the module caused the KMS lookup to flip? I think we changed provider selection to use an alias mapping per region (e.g., provider "aws" { alias = var.region == "us-west-2" ? "west" : "default" }).

dinesh: Yep — module now expects an external kms_key_id var instead of doing data.aws_kms_key lookups. In the canary we pass kms_id via terragrunt include, but the provider alias caused the data lookup to run in the wrong account/region.

maya: ops-oncall FYI we saw two symptoms: 1) failure to create instances (quota) 2) terraform plan shows provider drift. Runner logs: 

```bash
Error: error creating EBS volume: quota exceeded
...
Error: KMSNotFoundException: Key 'alias/redwood-gpupool' not found in us-west-2
```

ops-oncall: I've paused the GitOps pipeline for that repo and blocked merges to main. Reverting to module v0.11.2 pin until we sort provider alias semantics.

sasha: Suggested fix: change module to accept kms_key_arn and keep internal data lookup behind a `count = var.kms_key_arn == "" ? 1 : 0` so we don't double-read. But the bigger issue is provider selection: the new module started using `for_each` over regions with `providers = { aws = aws.regional[each.key] }` which breaks our terragrunt include patterns.

lee: We hit the same pattern in eu-west-1 when AZ affinity mapping uses `lookup(var.subnet_map, var.region)` and terraform crashed when provider alias wasn't wired. I can add a safety wrapper in our org-level module to normalize provider alias mapping before we upgrade.

dinesh: :eyes: Also need to check state migration — plan shows `module.gpufleet.aws_instance.gpu_pool` will be replaced due to provider config change. That replacement would recreate instances and could wipe PVs if applied without migration.

maya: Proposal: do a two-step rollout:
1) Add compatibility shim in infra repo that sets the provider aliases the new module expects (no state changes).
2) Run a dry-run canary in staging with the shim in place.
3) Apply lockfile + pin in module registry (prevent accidental major bumps).
4) Update production canary limited to a couple of pools then full rollout.

infra-bot: Reminder: terraform state lock is held by pipeline-4987 for ~12m. If you need to unlock, run `terraform force-unlock` from the maintainers group.

sasha: Also let's add an automated check in GitLab CI — a `tfcheck` job that validates provider.aliases exist in live envs before merge; and enforce that module bumps > major require a state-migration plan in the PR description.

ops-oncall: Cost note: during the failed run we created spot-fallback nodes in another region, usage spiked ~18% and finance flagged a $2k overrun. I'll file a ticket with finance and tag the cost center.

maya: Action items: @sasha add shim PR, @lee add TFCheck CI job, @dinesh draft state migration playbook, @ops-oncall follow up with finance. I'll unpause pipelines when shim is merged. :white_check_mark:
